groundTruth.description: Fixes GHSA-g3rq-g295-4j3m / CVE-2020-28493: the urlize() filter's punctuation-splitting regex (_punctuation_re, with nested quantifiers) was vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS) on crafted input. This commit replaces the single combined regex with a rewritten urlize() that does lead/tail stripping via separate, simpler anchored regexes (one anchored to the start, one to the end, explicitly avoiding mid-string backtracking per the added code comment) and inlines several previously-module-level precompiled patterns. This is a substantial rewrite (~80 changed lines in one function), not a minimal patch, which makes it a meaningfully harder known-fix case than 001/002/005: a reviewer must judge whether a large unfamiliar rewrite is safe, not just whether a one-line change is.

evidence.note: rewritten urlize() function and its new anchored regexes

runs.label: live run, Claude Code CLI 2.1.299, external repository input
runs.outcomeNote: All three reviewers completed with zero findings (status: complete, verdict: recommend-approval), correctly not flagging the new regexes as risky despite the function being substantially rewritten. Matches the known-fix ground truth.

notes: Preflight initially refused with BUDGET_EXCEEDED at the default policy template's maxInputTokensPerReviewer (100000): the combined prompt (utils.py, ~22KB, plus the loaded skill guidance text) came to ~101-103k tokens per role, just over the cap - not a product bug, just this file+skill combination needing more headroom than the default. Raised maxInputTokensPerReviewer to 120000 for this case only; documented here rather than silently matching the other cases' policy value, since a reader comparing policies across cases should know why this one differs.
